Saito_1971.independently_read_scope: Indexed Introduction states the main theorem for f in C{x_1,...,x_n} having an isolated singularity at0: if f=sum_i g_i*(partial_i f), with holomorphic g_i, there are local coordinates in which f is a quasihomogeneous polynomial.
Saito_1971.short_exact_quote: S'il existe g_1,...,g_n ... tels que f = g_1 partial f/partial x_1 + ... + g_n partial f/partial x_n, alors il existe un systeme de coordonnees locales dans lequel f est un polynome quasi-homogene.

Saito_1971.use: Standard isolated-hypersurface theorem is an explicit external input. Equality mu=tau implies f in its Jacobian ideal by comparing the finite Milnor algebra with its quotient by f. All local germs used here are reduced plane curves with isolated singularities.

Saito_1980.use: No inaccessible theorem is required for determinant criterion: the separate review proves the needed algebraic statement using Cramer's rule and tangency at the generic smooth point of each reduced factor.
